cards.explanation: The answer is the end. Amos says he sees a basket of summer fruit, and the LORD answers, "The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them." (Amos 8:2) Amos was just asked a simple question, and the answer was this. I think that basket stopped looking so pretty to him right then.

The answer is wailing. The Lord GOD says, "the songs of the temple will turn to wailing." (Amos 8:3) The music doesn't just get quieter, friends. It turns into something else completely. I think that's a sound nobody in that temple wanted to hear.

The answer is so they can sell grain. These people who trample the needy ask, "When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain?" (Amos 8:5) The New Moon and the Sabbath are in their way, and they're watching for when they end. I think this is a heavy verse, because their plan is to cheat people.

The answer is True. They say, "Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales." (Amos 8:5) That's three tricks in one sentence, friends. I think this is a heavy part, because it's a plan to cheat people.
The answer is False. The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: "I will never forget any of their deeds." (Amos 8:7) There's no "in time" in that sentence, friends. He says never, and He swore it.

The answer is the Nile. The land will "…swell like the Nile; it will surge and then subside like the Nile in Egypt." (Amos 8:8) That river rises and falls, and the whole land is pictured doing the same. Big movement, friends, all of it swelling and surging.

The answer is an only son. The LORD says, "I will make it like a time of mourning for an only son, and its outcome like a bitter day." (Amos 8:10) That's about as deep as grief gets, friends. I think this is a verse to read slowly.

The answer is words. The Lord GOD says it will be "…a famine of hearing the words of the LORD." (Amos 8:11) A full cupboard and a full glass won't help with that kind of hunger, friends. Some hunger only God's words can feed.

The answer is False. People will "…stagger from sea to sea and roam from north to east, seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it." (Amos 8:12) All that searching, and the finding doesn't happen. That's a long walk with nothing at the end of it, friends.

The answer is that they will fall and never rise again. The LORD says of those who swear by Samaria's guilt, Dan's god and the way of Beersheba, "…they will fall, never to rise again." (Amos 8:14) That's the end of the passage, friends. I think it's a serious way to close.
